The '''Murk system''' was a part of the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell subsector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]]. It contained the [[Red dwarf/Legends|red dwarf]] [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Murk (star)|Murk]], which was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by several [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoids]].

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] established the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]], a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] meant for the [[Transport/Legends|transportation]] of construction materials and components to the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], the Murk [[Star system/Legends|system]] became the penultimate stop on the [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] route. On the system's innermost planetoid, also named [[Murk (planetoid)|Murk]], an Imperial [[cargo-transfer station]] was established, where cargoes arriving via the Sanctuary Pipeline were unloaded for subsequent shipment to the Endor system. Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the [[Shell Hutts|Shell Hutt]] [[Tagoonta]] escaped to the Murk transfer station from troubles in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].

==Description==
The Murk system was situated in the [[Outer Moddell systems]] area of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell subsector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] constituting the [[Inner Zuma Region]]<ref name="TEA" /> of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]].<ref name="EAOC" />

The [[Star system/Legends|system]] contained the [[Red dwarf/Legends|red dwarf]]&ndash;type [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Murk (star)|Murk]], which, due to its dimness, was not visible to naked-[[Eye/Legends|eye]] observers on any of the Moddell subsector's inhabited [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. The star was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by several [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoids]], the innermost of which was an [[Atmosphere/Legends|airless]], [[Temperature/Legends|frigid]], barren rock of the [[Murk (planetoid)|same name]]. The latter took ninety-eight [[Local day/Legends|local days]] to complete an orbit around its sun.<ref name="Endor" />

==History==
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] began the construction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] over the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]], in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]. To allow for expeditious, secret [[Transport/Legends|transportation]] of the necessary materials and components to Endor, the Empire [[S-thread booster/Legends|artificially]] extended the [[Silvestri Trace]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] from<ref name="Endor" /> the [[Brema sector/Legends|Brema sector]]<ref name="EAOC Sullust">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]]</ref> planet<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]] directly to Endor,<ref name="Endor" /> with the Murk system becoming a penultimate stop on the new [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] route, known as the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Murk-TEAmap.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Murk system became the penultimate stop on the Sanctuary Pipeline.]]
To add another layer of secrecy to the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] project, an Imperial [[cargo-transfer station]] with both ground-based and orbital facilities was established on Murk, used to unload shipments arriving via the Sanctuary Pipeline for further transportation to the Endor system. Following the Imperial defeat by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Endor" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the Sanctuary Pipeline became largely [[Navigator/Legends|unnavigable]] and the Murk transfer station was abandoned. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the reign of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the [[Shell Hutts|Shell Hutt]] [[Tagoonta]] and his retainers found refuge at the transfer station from troubles in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="Endor" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Murk system was introduced via map label in the article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]," which was published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Endor" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' provided the system with a visual depiction and placed it in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />
